kurz: Fluffy means: lots of small gas bubbles that are held in place in the oven, and a batter tender enough not to be tough.
bild_im_kopf: Like a sponge with a thousand little holes instead of a brick.
bedeutung: Gas comes from baking powder, yeast, whisked egg whites or steam. It turns fluffy when the gas forms at the right moment and the batter sets before it escapes. Little [[glutenbildung|gluten network]] keeps the result tender.
was_passiert: Too much mixing makes it tough and drives the air back out. Too little [[triebmittel|raising agent]] or standing too long leaves the batter flat.
faustregeln: Combine dry and wet ingredients only briefly.
Fold in whisked egg whites gently.
Do not leave a batter with baking powder standing for long.

praxis.text: Pancakes: lumps in the batter are fine. Stirred smooth, they turn rubbery.
Soufflés and soufflé omelettes live entirely on whisked egg whites.
